story.title: Lindsay Clancy Trial Ends in Mistrial Due to Jury Deadlock
story.summary: The trial of Lindsay Clancy resulted in a mistrial as the jury could not reach a unanimous verdict. A holdout juror expressed reasonable doubt but stated he would not acquit Clancy. Other jurors described frustration during deliberations, revealing that some initially leaned towards a guilty verdict. Clancy's attorney plans to file a motion to dismiss the case following the mistrial.

timeline_highlights.title: Mistrial Declared in Lindsay Clancy's Murder Case After Jury Deadlocks
timeline_highlights.summary: Lindsay Clancy's murder trial ended in a mistrial after the jury was unable to reach a unanimous decision following five weeks of testimony and seven days of deliberation. Clancy is charged with the deaths of her three children, with her defense arguing she was suffering from postpartum psychosis, while prosecutors contended that the killings were premeditated. The outcome leaves Clancy's future and potential criminal liability uncertain.

event_overview.title: About Lindsay Clancy Case
event_overview.subject: Lindsay Clancy Case
event_overview.summary: The Lindsay Clancy case is a Massachusetts criminal prosecution arising from the deaths of Clancy’s three children in Duxbury on January 24, 2023. The central issue at her 2026 trial was criminal responsibility: the defense argued that mental illness left her not criminally responsible, while prosecutors argued that the Commonwealth could prove responsibility beyond a reasonable doubt.

facts.label: Incident and location
facts.value: Police and first responders were called to a home in Duxbury, Plymouth County, Massachusetts, on January 24, 2023; the three children were later pronounced dead. The Plymouth County District Attorney’s Office said the medical examiner found asphyxia or complications of asphyxia as the causes of death.

facts.label: Charges and plea
facts.value: Clancy pleaded not guilty at her February 7, 2023 arraignment. A Plymouth County grand jury returned indictments on September 15, 2023 charging three counts of murder and three counts of strangulation or suffocation.

facts.label: Court and legal framework
facts.value: The case was tried in Plymouth County Superior Court. Under Massachusetts’s criminal-responsibility standard, a person is not criminally responsible if, because of a mental disease or defect, they lacked substantial capacity to appreciate the wrongfulness of the conduct or to conform conduct to the law; once the issue is raised, the Commonwealth bears the burden to prove criminal responsibility beyond a reasonable do

facts.label: 2026 trial outcome
facts.value: The jury did not reach a unanimous verdict, and the judge declared a mistrial on September 4, 2026. A mistrial is not an acquittal; as of September 9, a decision on whether to seek another trial rested with the Plymouth County District Attorney’s Office.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the late-trial focus on psychiatric treatment and the jury deadlock/mistrial, rather than the full investigation, charging history, and all earlier proceedings since January 2023.
